title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page: Serre–Tate style deformation theory of an ordinary-type p-divisible group. M is étale, N is of multiplicative type ('de t.m.') or more generally radicial. Over a base S with closed subscheme S_0 (p nilpotent, infinitesimal thickening), the extensions of M by N that are trivialised over S_0 are classified by Ext^1(M,N). This set is represented by the formal torus G = T_p(M)^∨ ⊗ N, the twisted torus of the previous page. Concretely, an extension corresponds to a homomorphism T_p(M) → N(S) with values in the kernel of reduction, i.e. the Serre–Tate q-parameter.

This page treats the functoriality. Take a second pair M', N' with its torus G' = T_p(M')^∨ ⊗ N', and homomorphisms u: M → M' and v: N → N'. Grothendieck asks for pairs of extensions (E of M by N, E' of M' by N'), both trivialised over S_0, such that some homomorphism E → E' is compatible with u and v. He notes that such a homomorphism is then unique. This follows from rigidity: Hom(M,N') vanishes on the kernel of reduction.

Standard homological algebra gives the criterion. The required condition is v_*(ξ) = u^*(ξ') in Ext^1(M,N'). The maps v_*: Ext^1(M,N) → Ext^1(M,N') and u^*: Ext^1(M',N') → Ext^1(M,N') are induced by homomorphisms of formal tori into H = T_p(M)^∨ ⊗ N':
- α: G → H, induced by v;
- β: G' → H, induced by T_p(u)^∨.

Hence the locus of compatible pairs is represented by K = Ker(α − β : G × G' → H), the fibre product G ×_H G'. This is a formal subgroup of the product of the two tori, so it is again of multiplicative type.

Purpose, made explicit on the next page: apply this with E = E' (or E' the dual) and u, v coming from a polarisation or an endomorphism. One gets that the locus in the Serre–Tate formal moduli torus of an ordinary abelian variety where the polarisation (or homomorphism) lifts is a formal subgroup. So the formal moduli of ordinary polarised abelian varieties is again a formal group of multiplicative type, with the canonical (CM) lift at its origin.
errors: No real error. One minor gap: the kernel K of a homomorphism of formal tori need not be a torus. It is of multiplicative type but may have a finite or non-reduced part (e.g. a factor p in α − β), so 'formal group of multiplicative type' is the right statement, not 'formal torus'.
The uniqueness of the hom E → E' is asserted without proof. It holds by rigidity: Hom(M, N') restricted to the kernel of reduction is 0 when M is étale and N' is radicial/multiplicative.

ideas.what: Extensions of an étale p-divisible group by a multiplicative one, trivialised on S_0, are represented by the formal torus T_p(M)^∨ ⊗ N (Serre–Tate coordinates)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (1964 Woods Hole), exposed by Katz (1981), Messing (1972)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the 1966 letter to Tate on crystals and in Grothendieck's 1970 Montréal lectures (Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné), but unsure

ideas.what: Functoriality: compatible pairs of extensions (ξ, ξ') with v_*ξ = u^*ξ' form the kernel of α − β, a formal subgroup of G × G'
ideas.modern_name: Locus where a homomorphism lifts is a formal subgroup in Serre–Tate coordinates (linearity of Hecke/endomorphism loci)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz, 'Serre–Tate local moduli' (1981); later Moonen (PEL Serre–Tate theory), Chai (Tate-linear subvarieties)

ideas.what: Application to polarised ordinary abelian varieties: the formal moduli is a formal group of multiplicative type, with the canonical (CM) lift as origin
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate canonical lifting; group structure on the deformation space of ordinary polarised AVs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate; Messing; Katz; Deligne (ordinary AVs over finite fields)

missed.claim: A 1966 unpublished formulation, prior to Katz 1981, of the fact that loci where homomorphisms (in particular polarisations) lift form formal subgroups of the Serre–Tate torus. It is obtained as the kernel of α − β for the pullback/pushforward maps on Ext^1.
missed.quote: le noyau K de G × G' ⇉ H, (ce dernier représente infinitésimalement le système des [couples (ξ, ξ')])
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only: the statement is well known (Katz, Moonen, Chai) and was circulating in Serre–Tate/Tate correspondence. This is a record of Grothendieck's independent treatment.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean, correct functoriality argument for Serre–Tate coordinates. The content is standard and later published by Katz and others, though the page documents Grothendieck working it out in 1966.
transcription_corrections: The garbled 'Ğ ... Ḧ' fragments should read: the homs v_* and u^* are 'représentés' by homomorphisms of formal groups α: G = T_p(M)^∨⊗N → H = T_p(M)^∨⊗N' (defined by v) and β: G' = T_p(M')^∨⊗N' → H (defined by u).

'si on considère H i.e. de α−β, le noyau K de G × G' ⇉ H' should read roughly: 'si on considère le noyau K de α − β : G × G' → H, ce dernier représente infinitésimalement le système des [couples (ξ, ξ')]'.
'(ce dernier est alors unique)' refers to the hom E → E'.
